semanticText:
# Shipment Clause

Prepares and selects one embedded shipping-instruction document. It tracks preparation, provider submission, participant admission and document readiness. `selected` and `usable` do not establish dispatch, delivery or carrier acceptance.

## Bindings and configuration

- `instruction` is the required destination binding: a non-root JSON Pointer with no default path. The selected instruction is embedded there. `cardinality` is `single`; preparation uses the key `single` and rejects another key.
- `parties` is an object of party mappings, defaulting to `{}`. Preparation requires a nonempty mapping. The prepared instruction must declare `carrier` under `/clauses/activation/parameters/parties`.
- `sources` is an object of source mappings, defaulting to `{}`. A mapping to `self` can require admission of candidate participants into the host document. Source-declaration planning combines template-level `sources` with declarations in template clauses and rejects conflicting declarations for the same alias.
- `template` is an optional non-root pointer binding. When supplied, planning requires its target to exist and captures a snapshot. Source-declaration planning also reads `parameters.template`; the complete template-resolution rules are not supplied.

`obtain` defaults to `create` and accepts only `create` or `provide`. Provider mode requires `suppliedBy`, identifying the caller allowed to supply the instruction. `suppliedParties` defaults to an empty list and identifies party roles the provider may fill; a nonempty list is rejected in create mode.

`specialization/dataPaths` defaults to an empty list. Its entries must identify existing data slots, avoid reserved document structure, and neither duplicate nor overlap other slots. Specialization remains subject to the shipment-specific checks below.

The prepared document must pass the shipping-instruction type check. Its `shipmentTerms`, read as `{}` when absent, are frozen in the preparation record as `domainTerms`. A supplied candidate must have exactly matching `shipmentTerms`, also read as `{}` when absent; otherwise provision fails with `SHIPMENT_TERMS_MISMATCH`. The supplied evidence does not define the internal shipment terms or shipping execution fields.

## Actions and recorded outcomes

Preparation records reside under `/process_{clauseKey}/entries/*`. Planning initializes `entries` to `{}`. Missing state does not establish readiness or completion.

**`prepare`** accepts construction inputs `fields` and `values`, each defaulting to `{}`, plus `key` and `requestId`. The key defaults to `single`; `requestId` defaults to that key and must be nonempty text. Its preflight treats an existing identical intent—configuration, template identity, request identifier, fields and values—as a duplicate. A different intent for the same entry is rejected, as is an occupied destination for a new preparation.

In create mode, preparation writes the prepared instruction to `instruction`, records `documentOrigin`, and sets `selected`. Initialization and readiness remain separate. In provide mode, it records `awaiting_provider` and emits a provision request identifying `suppliedBy`, `requestId` and `requirementRef`. That request does not confirm that an instruction has been supplied.

**`provide`** requires an existing provider-mode preparation and a call channel matching the stored `supplier`. `inResponseTo` must match `requestId`, and `requirementRef` must match the frozen preparation requirement. By default, these fields and `document` come from the trigger, falling back to empty strings; `key` falls back to `single`. Valid provision requires an initialized document publication.

Provision checks the initialized original against the reviewed preparation, allowing only configured specialization, and checks the effective clause policy, party continuity, declared party roster, required approval policy and frozen shipment terms. Supplied data slots must satisfy their declarations and remain unchanged between the initialized original and the submitted publication. Stored `prepareFor` controls additional validation: `bootstrap` invokes bootstrap party and access checks; missing stored mode is read as `inherited`. The helper selecting the configured preparation mode is not supplied.

A provider candidate's original identity is retained as `candidateOrigin`; later submissions cannot substitute another origin. A candidate can be recorded as `admission_pending`, `awaiting_activation` or `linking` before selection. `ready` is an intermediate validation result: `sharedProvide` then installs the candidate reference at `instruction`, records `documentOrigin`, and stores `selected`. A selected origin cannot be replaced. A matching already-selected submission can be a duplicate, subject to the provision checks.

**`resume`** refreshes entries that already have `documentOrigin`; it does not select a staged provider candidate. Destination changes and embedded-document events also invoke this refresh. Once the selected instruction is initialized, its original identity must match the recorded origin. Refresh records `usable` only when the instruction's `/activation/active` is true and `namedSourcesReady` succeeds; a later failed readiness check can restore `selected`. The shipment-specific `domainNextActions` returns an empty list. `resume` can return `acceptedNew` even when no state changes.

**`cancel`** requires an existing preparation without `documentOrigin`. It records `cancellation_requested` and emits a cancellation request; repeating that request is a duplicate. A selected instruction requires domain cancellation instead. Provision is blocked for `cancellation_requested`, `cancelled`, `admission_denied` and `reapproval_required`. The supplied functions recognize `cancelled` in this guard but do not show a transition confirming cancellation.

The four actions have no automatic connection declared by this type. Configured connections can use authenticated workflows, channels, events, initialization, activation, changes, embedded documents, collections or timers. Connection `params` override action defaults; `when` defaults to true and `once` to false. Failed requirements or action conditions reject execution. Non-`acceptedNew` preflight outcomes stop before action effects; non-`acceptedNew` action outcomes stop before `after` effects and `once` completion. Thus `acceptedNew` can mean that a candidate was staged or a request recorded, without confirming an external outcome.

Timer connections use either an absolute `timestamp` in Unix microseconds or `afterEvent` with a positive integer `delayMs`. Relative `policy` defaults to `first`, which ignores further arms once armed; `latest` allows rescheduling. `cancelOn` emits a timer-cancellation request.

## Participant admission

When a `self` source mapping requires candidate participants absent from the host roster, preparation requires configured admission approvers and candidate access documents for those participants. Approvers must be distinct declared host parties. The admission token binds the candidate, requirement, participants, access scope and host activation revision.

`admission_pending` can await configured approval, each incoming party's explicit `approve` consent, and access validation for the expanded roster. Approval requires exact document-version review. Installation additionally requires approved history, a matching grant and the unchanged activation revision. Access requests are requests, not evidence that access has been granted. Any recorded `decline` produces `admission_denied`; a changed host activation revision requires renewed review through `reapproval_required`.

Installation uses `installing`. Completion verifies that the host roster covers the incoming parties, records `admittedRevision`, and stores `linking`; the emitted `admitted` notification is distinct from the stored status. Candidate source checks require initialized sources with matching origins, roster coverage and active status before selection. A staged candidate must pass provision again to advance to selection; readiness refresh alone does not do this.

An admission approver can rebase a current `reapproval_required` admission with exact document-version review and the matching `admissionRef`. Rebase clears the old token and consents, increments the admission attempt, and returns the entry to `awaiting_provider` while retaining its candidate-origin commitment. Retired admissions preserve their reason, token and recorded consents.

Document-access registration accepts one to sixteen initialized Timeline Access publications. It requires exact document-version review and a caller channel present in the host party roster, then delegates installation to the access helper. The detailed access and activation helper rules are not supplied.

When invoked, the preparation transition validator rejects the proposed transition with `PREPARATION_IMMUTABLE_WHILE_OBLIGATIONS_EXIST`; its supplied implementation returns `allowed: false` without a conditional exception.
